summary: 埃克曼从一段病人访谈中发现短暂表情可能泄露被隐藏的情绪。文章追踪这项研究怎样进入专业训练和电视，并交代研究者关注的是哪些谎言。

paragraphs.brief: 一个精神科临床问题的起点
sentences: Forty years ago, the research psychologist Dr Paul Ekman was addressing a group of young psychiatrists in training when he was asked a question, the answer to which has kept him busy ever since.
四十年前，心理学研究者保罗·埃克曼在给一群受训的年轻精神科医生讲话时，被问到了一个他此后一直在研究的问题。
Suppose the group wanted to know whether a particular patient who swears they are telling the truth really is.
这些医生想知道，如果病人发誓说的是真话，该怎样判断？
They look and sound sincere.
病人的表情和声音都可能显得真诚。
So here is the question: is there any way you can be sure they are telling the truth?
那么，问题就在这里：你是否有办法确定他们说的是实话？
Ekman did not know the answer then, but he wanted to find out.
埃克曼当时不知道答案但他想找出答案
paragraphs.gist: 年轻精神科医生问，面对言语和神情都诚恳的病人，怎样知道对方是否说了真话，这一问题由此成为埃克曼长期研究的起点。

paragraphs.brief: 放慢录像发现短暂微表情
sentences: As part of his research, he had already filmed a series of 12-minute interviews with psychiatric patients.
作为研究的一部分，他已经拍摄了一系列12分钟的采访精神病患者。
In a subsequent conversation, one of the patients told him that she had lied to him.
在随后的谈话中，一名病人告诉他，她对他撒谎。
So Ekman sat and looked at the film but saw nothing noteworthy.
于是埃克曼坐下来看访谈录像，一开始没有发现异常。
Then he slowed it down and looked again.
他把录像放慢，重新看了一遍。
Then he slowed it down even further.
接着，他又放慢了一点。
And suddenly, there, across just two frames of the film, he saw it: an intense expression of extreme anguish.
突然，他在连续两帧画面中看到了极度痛苦的表情。
It lasted less than a fifteenth of a second, but once he had spotted the first expression, he soon found three more examples in that same interview.
这个表情持续不到十五分之一秒，但发现第一次以后，他很快又在同一次访谈里找到了三次。
He termed his discovery “micro-expressions”: very rapid, intense demonstrations of emotion that the subject intended to conceal.
他把这类现象叫作“微表情”：一个人试图掩饰的强烈情绪在脸上一闪而过。
paragraphs.gist: 埃克曼反复放慢一名承认说谎者的访谈录像，在仅两帧中看到了转瞬即逝的痛苦神情，遂将此类试图隐藏的情绪信号称为微表情。

paragraphs.brief: 七种基本情绪的跨文化证据
sentences: Over the course of the next four decades, Ekman successfully demonstrated a proposition first suggested by Charles Darwin: that the ways in which we express rage, disgust, contempt, fear, surprise, happiness and sadness are universal.
在今后40年中，埃克曼成功地展示了查尔斯·达尔文首先提出的一个主张：我们表达愤怒、厌恶、蔑视、恐惧、惊讶、幸福和悲伤的方式是普遍的。
The facial muscles triggered by those seven basic emotions are, he has shown, essentially standard, regardless of language and culture, from the US to Japan and Brazil to Papua New Guinea.
他已证明，从美国到日本，从巴西到巴布亚新几内亚，无论语言和文化有何差异，这七种基本情绪调动的面部肌肉基本相同。

What is more, expressions of emotion are impossible to suppress and, particularly when we are lying, micro-expressions of powerfully felt emotions will inevitably flit across our face before we get the chance to stop them.
强烈的情绪很难完全压住，尤其是撒谎时，一个人还没来得及控制，微表情已经在脸上掠过。
paragraphs.gist: 埃克曼的跨文化研究认为，七种基本情绪由相似的面部肌肉表达，内心强烈的感受有时会在能有意识抑制之前短暂显露。

paragraphs.brief: 从少数天才到辨认训练
sentences: Fortunately for liars, most people will fail to spot these fleeting signals of inner torment.
幸运的是，对骗子来说，大多数人将无法发现这些瞬息万变的内心痛苦的信号。
Of the 15 000 Ekman has tested, only 50 people, whom he calls “naturals”, have been able to do it.
在埃克曼测试的一万五千人中，只有五十人能自行辨认这些信号，他称他们为“天生的识谎者”。
But given a little more training, Ekman says, almost anyone can develop the skill.
但埃克曼说，只要稍加训练，几乎人人都能学会这项技能。

He should know: since these tests were completed in the mid-1980s and the first publication of his research, he has been called in by the FBI and CIA (among countless more law-enforcement and other agencies around the world), not just to solve cases, but to teach them how to use his technique for themselves.
他对此很有发言权：自从八十年代中期完成测试并首次发表研究，美国联邦调查局和中央情报局等世界各地众多机构，就请他协助破案并传授识别方法。
He has held workshops for defence and prosecution lawyers, health professionals, even jealous spouses, all of them wanting to know exactly when someone is not being 100 percent candid.
辩护律师、检察官、医护人员，甚至心生猜疑的配偶，都参加过他的讲习班，希望判断别人何时没有说出全部实情。
paragraphs.gist: 受试的一万五千人中只有五十人天生善于发现这些信号，但埃克曼认为这项技能可训练，执法人员、律师和医护人员也向他学习。

paragraphs.brief: 电视剧夸大测谎的风险
sentences: Most recently, Ekman’s research has resulted in a new television series about the exploits of the fictional Dr Cal Lightman, a scientist who studies involuntary body language to discover not only if you are lying, but why you might have been motivated to do so.
最近，他的研究还催生了一部电视剧，主人公是虚构的科学家卡尔·莱特曼博士，他根据无意识的肢体语言判断别人是否在说谎，还试图找出动机。
According to the publicity blurb, Lightman is a human lie detector, even more accurate than a polygraph test.
宣传词把莱特曼形容成一台比测谎仪还准确的“人体测谎器”。
Ekman concedes he was sceptical when the producer first approached him with the idea of turning his life’s work into a TV series, and initially would have stopped the project if he could.
埃克曼承认，制片人最初提议将他一生的研究改编成电视剧时，他颇为怀疑，要是能作主，他当时可能会叫停这个项目。

In particular, he was fearful that the show would exaggerate the effectiveness of his techniques and create the quite inaccurate impression among audiences that criminals could no longer hope to get away with lying.
特别是，他担心这次表演会夸大其技巧的效力，给观众造成一种相当不准确的印象，即犯罪分子再也不能指望说谎而逃脱惩罚。

In the worst-case scenario, he was concerned about unfair convictions—that one day someone not properly trained in his techniques might be sitting on a jury and wrongly find someone guilty of a crime simply on the basis of a television programme.
在最坏的情况下，他担心的是不公正的定罪——有一天，在他的技术方面没有受过适当训练的人可能坐在陪审团里，仅仅根据电视节目就错误地认定某人犯有罪行。
paragraphs.gist: 以他的研究为蓝本的电视剧把主角写成“人体测谎仪”，埃克曼起初担心夸大准确性，尤其怕陪审员因模仿电视而误判。

sentences: In the end, though, he was won over because the series is unusual in several respects.
最后他被说服了，因为这部剧在几个方面确实与众不同。
It is the first time, as far as Ekman is aware, that a commercial TV drama has been based on the work of just one scientist.
据埃克曼所知，这是商业电视剧首次取材于一名科学家的研究工作。
That scientist is also deeply involved in the project, talking through plot ideas and checking five successive drafts of each script to ensure details are correct.
他本人也深度参与创作，讨论情节构思，并逐一审看每集剧本的五版稿件，以确保细节准确。
He was also impressed with the producer’s manifestly serious and well-intentioned reasons for making the programme.
制片人认真而善意的初衷也打动了他。
Now that the first series has been completed, he believes probably 80–90 per cent of the show is based on fact and that’s good enough for what it is.
第一季拍完后，他估计大约八至九成内容有事实依据，作为剧情剧已经足够。
After all, it is a drama, not a documentary.
毕竟，这是一个戏剧，不是纪录片。
paragraphs.gist: 制作方让埃克曼参与情节讨论并反复审阅剧本，使他最终接受了合作，也认为这部商业剧的大部分内容在事实层面站得住脚。

paragraphs.brief: 什么样的欺骗才算说谎
sentences: Ekman, incidentally, professes to have been a terrible liar ever since he was a small boy and observes that the ability to detect a lie and the ability to lie successfully are completely unrelated.
顺带一提，埃克曼自称从小就不擅长撒谎，并指出识破谎言与把谎话说得令人信服是两项毫无关联的能力。
He has been asked by people running for high office if he could teach them to become more credible with the public but has always refused to use his skills in that way on ethical grounds.
曾有竞逐公职的人请他传授赢得公众信任的方法，他始终出于道德考虑而拒绝。
He also insists that there are various kinds of lies.
他还坚持认为，存在着各种各样的谎言。
A “true” lie can be identified by having two essential characteristics: there must be a deliberate intent to mislead and there must be no notification that this is what is occurring.
他认为，真正的谎言有两项特征：说话者有意误导，而且不会预先告知对方自己正在这样做。
This means that an actor or a poker player isn’t a true liar.
这表示演员或扑克玩家不是真正的骗子。
They are supposed to deceive you—it’s part of the game—and the same is true of flattery.
人们本就预期演员和牌手会设法骗过自己，这是游戏规则的一部分；恭维话也是如此。
He prefers to focus on the kinds of lies where the liar would be in grave trouble if they were found out, and where the target would feel properly aggrieved if they knew.
他更关注的是后果严重的谎言：一旦被识破，说谎者会惹上大麻烦，受骗者也有充分理由感到受伤或愤慨。
paragraphs.gist: 埃克曼区分识破与编造谎言的能力，坚持真正的说谎须有意误导且不预先告知，所以演戏、打牌和他关注的高风险欺骗性质不同。

items.en: According to the writer, Ekman became interested in lying after a question from his
items.zh: 据作者所说，埃克曼是因为谁提出的一个问题，而开始对说谎这一现象产生研究兴趣的？

items.en: The writer refers to the 12-minute interviews in order to
correct: describe the origins of Ekman’s theories.
描述艾克曼理论的起源。

items.en: What is the writer’s point in the third paragraph?
items.zh: 作者在第三段中有什么观点？
correct: Micro-expressions are common to all people.
微表情是人类共有的现象。

items.en: What are we told about Ekman’s conclusions from his tests?
items.zh: 我们如何得知Ekman的测试结论？
correct: Few untrained people can detect lying.
没有受过训练的人很少能察觉到说谎

items.en: What point does the writer make about Ekman’s techniques in the fourth paragraph?
items.zh: 作者在第四段对艾克曼的技巧有什么看法？
correct: They have been in great demand.
许多人和机构都需要这些技术。

items.en: Initially, Ekman was unenthusiastic about the TV project because he feared the possibility of encouraging viewers’ ________.
items.zh: 埃克曼起初对这部电视节目不太热心，因为他担心它可能加深观众的 ________。
items.why: 他担心观众形成错误观念 (false beliefs),故 32 = C false beliefs。

items.en: For example, he was worried that one day the programme could result in ________ not being carried out.
items.zh: 例如，他担心有一天，这部节目会导致 ________ 无法得到伸张。
items.why: 该情形意味着 justice 可能得不到伸张,33 = E justice。

items.en: Ultimately, though, he has given the show his blessing because he is not aware of any other comparable programme based on a single person’s ________.
items.zh: 不过，埃克曼最终还是支持了这部节目，因为据他所知，还没有同类节目以一个人的 ________ 为基础。
items.why: 值得赞许之处是节目基于单个人的研究,34 = H research。

items.en: The ________ of the show’s producer have been another pleasant surprise considering the genre of the programme.
items.zh: 考虑到这部节目的类型，制作人的 ________ 也是一个令人愉快的意外。
items.why: 让他惊喜的是制片人的动机,35 = D motives。

items.en: Ekman is happy with the show’s overall ________.
items.zh: 埃克曼对这部节目整体的 ________ 感到满意。
items.why: 他满意的是整体准确性,36 = F accuracy。

groups.label: 选词填空
groups.instructionsZh: 阅读带空格的中译，回想正确词项及其字母。

items.en: Ekman regrets the lies he told as a child.
items.zh: 艾克曼后悔他小时候说的谎言
items.why: 埃克曼说自己从小就很不擅长说谎。这说明的是说谎的能力，没有说他后悔童年说过的谎。

items.en: People who are good at lying tend to be good at detecting lies.
items.zh: 善于说谎的人往往善于发现谎言
items.why: 埃克曼明确说，成功说谎的能力与识破谎言的能力毫无关联，不能从擅长撒谎推出也擅长识谎。

items.en: Ekman has worked with poker players to help them lie more convincingly.
items.zh: Ekman和扑克牌手合作帮助他们更可信地撒谎
items.why: 扑克牌手是埃克曼用来解释“真正的谎言”的例子，因为玩家预期彼此设法误导。举例不能证明他曾训练牌手说谎。

items.en: Ekman is more interested in the types of lies with serious consequences.
items.zh: Ekman更关心那些具有严重后果的谎言
items.why: 他更关注后果严重的谎言，与题干一臻 YES.

groups.label: 观点判断 · YES / NO / NOT GIVEN

pairs: universal 在这里指人类普遍具有，概括不同人表达基本情绪的共同之处。
题干选项说观众形成“错误认识”，原文具体说节目可能让观众对识谎效果产生不准确的印象。
he is not aware of any other comparable programme
It is the first time, as far as Ekman is aware
“他不知道还有同类节目”对应“据他所知是第一次”，两种表达都保留了判断范围。
第 2 段 · 第 7 句
points: 埃克曼说自己从小就很不擅长说谎。这说明的是说谎的能力，没有说他后悔童年说过的谎。
该情形意味着 justice 可能得不到伸张,33 = E justice。
clauses: Forty years ago, the research psychologist Dr Paul Ekman was addressing a group of young psychiatrists in training when he was asked a question, the answer ….
“to which has kept him busy ever since”修饰前面的 answer。先认出先行词，再读从句补充的特征。
读到 which 时，回看 answer，再把修饰信息接回主句。
In a subsequent conversation, one of the patients told him ….
“that she had lied to him”补足 told 的内容，交代究竟在说、判断或发现什么。
先读 told 所在的主句，再把 that 后面的内容作为一个整体。
lead: Do tiny changes of facial expression show whether someone is telling lies?
面部表情的微小变化是否显示某人在说谎？
